desk.headline: Revenue up 4% to $324.6m but player costs cut EPS to $0.15, below $0.36 estimate; no guidance

other.label: Per-share note
other.value: EPS applies to all share series (A, B, C)

results: Total revenue rose 4% to $324.6m, led by ticket and event sales; average regular-season attendance rose 14%.
Media revenue fell 4% to $76.1m on the timing of BravesVision distribution income versus the old local TV deal.
Baseball operating costs jumped 16%, mainly higher player salaries and BravesVision production; adjusted OIBDA fell 40% to $40.6m.
Battery Atlanta (mixed-use) revenue grew 7% to $29.1m on higher rent, but its adjusted OIBDA slipped to $17.6m from $19.8m.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.15 from $0.47; cash was $121.5m and total debt $815.1m at 30 September.

guidance.summary: The company gives no financial guidance. On the call, management said BravesVision should beat the old local TV deal's yearly revenue, and free cash flow should normalise early in Q2 2027.

points: CEO Terry McGuirk said the higher payroll was a deliberate decision to invest in the roster.
CFO Jill Robinson asked that BravesVision be judged on a full-year basis, as its revenue timing differs from the old TV deal.
BravesVision costs in Q4 should be light versus Q3's $12.2m; Q4 will include the last three postseason home games.
Management described Battery Atlanta as a year-round income stream, not tied to the baseball season.
On debt, the CFO said the company is not forced to refinance mixed-use loans in the current market.
call.source: Earnings call transcript: Atlanta Braves Holdings misses Q3 2026 EPS forecast — Investing.com, 2026-11-04
